title: Which drift-alert setting an irrigation consortium's agro-climatic station network should run in 2028 so that drift alerts fit the field plan's visits, and how many a year it will raise, beside each district's 2027 drift-alert visits, the days their alerts waited and its breakdown visits at the stations kept
subdomain: sensor-calibration-measurement (the daily spatial-consistency check of a station network's air temperature: inverse-distance estimates from the nearest reporting stations, a 14-day drift statistic, limits from its recorded spread)
prompt_shape: 04: one dial (four settings), each setting's alerts a year, the setting and its count, beside per-district audit figures of the field visits and a chart of the settings against the budget
stated_inputs: the 28 drift-alert visits of the field plan

sources.origin: generated by task250/generator/make.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional consortium of irrigation communities in Aragon running 148 agro-climatic stations: a daily air-temperature field with a mesoscale part that decorrelates over tens of kilometres and winter inversions, station noise, sensor drifts each set right at the visit its alert sent or at the spring calibration round, the quality control's inverse-distance estimates and 14-day drift statistic, the alerts at setting 3.0, two maintenance contractors' work orders, the calibration database's transfer-standard readings, the register with its sensor history, the documents and the request; the consortium, the stations, the contractors and every person are invented, the quality-control method follows published spatial-consistency practice for surface station networks, and no real dataset is reproduced.
